newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-FERRARI TO POWER SAUBER FOR NEXT TWO YEARS.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-FERRARI TO POWER SAUBER FOR NEXT TWO YEARS.

text.p: Ferrari engines will be used to power the Sauber Formula One team in 1997 and 1998, the Swiss team announced on Monday.
Sauber said they had reached agreement with Ferrari to "manufacture, supply and develop" a Formula One engine for them.
The decision follows repeated denials by Ferrari that they will become involved in any further deals to supply engines to other teams after disappointing results with Scuderia Italia two seasons ago.

This time, Ferrari are setting up an independent working group and a seperate structure to work in relationship with Sauber's newly-created special engineering group, sponsored by Malaysia's national oil company Petronas.

Former Honda engine guru Osamo Goto has been appointed as the head of the new Sauber Petronas Engineering group. He was project leader with Honda from 1986 to 1990, when they powered five championship winners, and has been with Ferrari for the last three years.
Elsewhere, veteran British Formula One driver Martin Brundle said he feared his grand prix career could be over if the Jordan team succeed in signing Frenchman Jean Alesi.
Alesi is currently with Benetton, but was said on Monday to be meeting team chief Flavio Briatore to discuss his future after a disappointing end to his first season with them.
"There is nowhere else I want to go and nothing else I want to do, but drive the Jordan next year," said Brundle during a break in testing for the British RAC Rally.
"But it hit me the other day that Suzuka might have been my last grand prix and was a bit of a shock actually because I haven't really confronted that before.
"But I don't think it will be -- so don't write me off just yet."
